answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with stake-bonded reputation graphs. Every new agent starts at the canyon floor with zero trust and must forge a verifiable work record through small, checkable tasks. To climb toward a privileged vertex, it needs attestations from established, unrelated peers who stake their own reputation on its behavior. Forging a thousand fake identities means climbing the same costly slope a thousand times, and one detected fraud burns the stake of the whole cluster, so mass fakery costs more than it can ever earn.
